thread:
pagerduty: :warning: Alert: sustained elevation in streaming p99 latency in us-west-2 for 7m. Metric: streaming.end_to_end_latency.p99 > 750ms. Service: proxy-stream-router. Assigned: rachel.

rachel: I'm looking at traces and saw a sudden increase in in-flight streaming connections. Kernel hot-swap logs show repeated re-allocs. Non-stream API paths are normal.

devon: We're seeing many long-lived SSE connections holding onto KV cache entries; eviction and rehydration are spiking CPU on the servicers. This looks like a traffic pattern change, maybe a service started fan-out.

nate: Proxy write buffers filling -> clients getting 502s on streaming frames. Quick mitigation options: lower streaming window, apply per-tenant conn cap, or turn off SSE push so clients fall back to poll. Turning off push is fastest.

rachel: For immediate stabilization, I propose: (A) disable streaming pushes in us-west-2; (B) add 45s grace backoff header for clients; (C) apply tenant-level connection cap of 2; (D) notify CS so they can message impacted accounts. Anyone object?

ton y: No objections. Need eng-sre stamp. Also watch for negative UX where SDKs assume streaming. We should inject an 'X-Stream-Mode: disabled' header so SDKs can switch gracefully.

deploy-bot: Command ready:
```
redwoodctl feature toggle --name=push-streaming --region=us-west-2 --state=off --reason='latency mitigation'
```
Requires an eng-sre approval.

ops-bot: Runbook: streaming-fallback-rapid. Steps: toggle region, apply throttles, inject fallback header, spin dedicated pool for high-priority tenants if requested.

rachel: Devon, can you run the toggle? CS-lead, please prep outbound. Nate, apply conn cap.

devon: Executing toggle at 14:02:03 UTC:
```
> redwoodctl feature toggle --name=push-streaming --region=us-west-2 --state=off
status: success
op: f7d92
```
Initial telemetry shows backlog draining.

nate: Applying connection cap rule:
```
throttler set --scope=us-west-2 --rule=tenant_conn_limit --value=2
```
Result: ok (rule-id: r-22c).

cs-lead: Draft sent to affected tenants: "Temporary suspension of streaming pushes in us-west-2 to restore latency. Polling endpoints remain available. We'll provide updates every 30 minutes." Top-8 notified. Two replies asking for ETA, one requests isolated stream path.

ton y: Noted client asks. We can provision an isolated small stream pool for critical tenants with strict limits. That buys them streaming while protecting shared capacity.

rachel: Could we also reduce server-side keepalive for streaming connections to free sockets faster? Suggest reduce from 300s -> 60s as a temporary measure.

devon: Changing keepalive TTL now:
```
proxy-config set --region=us-west-2 --param=stream_keepalive_seconds --value=60
```
Applied (job: keep-9). Should reduce lingered sockets.

op s-bot: Note: header injection recommended to reduce client errors. Use X-Stream-Fallback: poll; also set Retry-After where appropriate.

nate: Injecting headers for matching SDK user agents. Job hdr-41 applied.

rachel: Metrics update: p99 dropped from ~830ms -> ~140ms within 75s. CPU on stream workers trending down. Good immediate signal. Keep measures in place for 1 hour then attempt a 2% re-enable canary.

cs-lead: One enterprise tenant asked for exception. We can offer: dedicated pool + conn limit 1 + instrumented canary. They accepted. Who will stand this up?

devon: I can provision a small dedicated pool (reserved g4-small) and bind the tenant. ETA ~10m. I'll annotate the instance with 'incident:2060001111'.

ton y: Also add a traffic-shape rule so their sessions are spread across workers to avoid single-worker overload.

devon: Dedicated pool spun up and bound to tenant-88. Limits: max-conns=1, rps=30. Observing tenant test traffic now.

rachel: Watch for client-facing errors. If we see >3% increase in 5xx for polling or fallback errors, roll back to previous mitigations and escalate.

nate: Small number of clients returning 'expected streaming frame' errors after toggle. Fallback header and SDK UA matching has mitigated most. Logging shows ~1.7% increased application-level warnings.

rachel: Oncall handoff: I need to step away in 30m. Devon, can you take lead during the stabilization window and own the canary?

devon: I will take the lead. Checklist for canary re-enable: 2% traffic, monitor p99, CPU, queue depth, and client error rate. Thresholds: p99 <300ms, client errors <1%, no queue growth trend. Immediate rollback on violation.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0784 | severity: high | mitigation summary: push streaming disabled in us-west-2, connection caps and keepalive reduced, fallback headers injected, dedicated pool for tenant-88. Owner: devon.

rachel: Thanks all. Leaving detailed notes in the incident doc. Devon, please post updates every 15m.

devon: Will do. Keeping this thread as the primary coordination channel. (react: rachel :white_check_mark:)
